This game is like a more polished version of Warframe. As an example, the game told me I had a 20% chance to get a particular item for a character and, after an hour, I finally got it. It was more like a 5% chance.  I have other games to play that are far more respectful of my time and wallet.

Don't get me wrong, it can be enjoyable at times. The predatory monetization just ruins it for me after a bit of playtime.

I am a 58 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for his birthday in 2024 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 40 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching Ukrainian men French kissing canines on YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

**Steam Deck review **

This game deserves a go for any fellow Steam Deck players; it takes some tinkering but once you’ve found the balance, it’s pretty smooth, and pretty good fun. 

Good points:
- with tinkering it runs well. 
- it’s similar in premise to Destiny (OG). 
- it’s seamless to play with others. 
- gunplay is good, world is good. 
- you can hop in and enjoy, hop out!

Negative points:
- text / maps are slightly difficult to read on the deck. 
- because of this, it can be difficult to follow. 
- it’s a pretty intensive game, graphically. 
- potential for ‘pay to win’ element. 

For anyone interested, I’m running relatively smooth 35-40FPS using the following in-game settings:

Preset: Low (except antialiasing - medium),
Motion Blur: Off,
Additional options: AMD, balanced,
V-Sync: Off,
Maximum Frame Rate: 40.

If you liked warframe, you will enjoy this. Very easy on the eyes. Maybe a bit pricier than Warframe but you can finish the game (main quest) without spending any money.

Gameplay: This is generally fine until you get normal or elite enemies with dumb modifiers like headshot only + extra health, make all other nearby enemies invincible (not an issue if you use AoE attacks). It gets extra annoying when the headshot only modifier gets added to an enemy whose head only shows in the front and they face away from you.

Movement: I've played lots of Warframe so I am biased about this topic BUT seeing this game try to push the parkour onto players when it's not refined is annoying, they even go as far as to add a grappling hook correction.

LASERS.. Oh boy, they add lasers to parkour sections or as a little time-based puzzles and the knockdown is actually insane, funny to see others get hit by it but annoying when you get super knocked into 2+ other lasers since their knockdown is VERY disruptive and displaces you immensely.

BOSSES: A lot of the world bosses have annoying orbs or mobs between phases, both grant invincibility and sometimes the orbs have extra gimmicks like: Destroy them in the order they spawned in or else they all respawn AT THE END, another is the orbs have invincibility windows so you have to switch targets constantly which isn't fun since they aren't exactly easy to hit being all small and moving around + with the boss.

VOID INTERCEPT BOSSES, I think they are fine but I just did Hanged Man and it has gimmicks that aren't clear. One guy complained to me for picking up a cube most people didn't know what to do and there is a point where it one shots everyone causing an immediate fail. Only reason I beat Hanged Man after a few tries is because it didn't do any of the gimmicks. This is an issue of the game being unclear for what to do. The other bosses weren't as bad and are clear so I HOPE future void intercept bosses are either more clear and/or don't rely on unfun gimmicks.

Story: I skipped pretty much all of the story so I will not judge the game on that aspect. I will say that dialogue during gameplay is good as to not draw out the time it takes to beat the game but I also didn't pay attention to it so I don't know if it was well done or not.

Farm: Farming is generally unfun if it's too tedious. Warframe has been transitioning into an extra farm specific resource so you are guaranteed to get what you want. In Warframe Jade for example if you spam the mission with her drops also grant a unique resource. If you play long enough and don't get her drops off RNG you can instead use the resource to claim her parts or for whatever else unique drops in that mission. I've been farming Blair in this game for 2 days so that 20% drop rate looks like a lie. I still haven't receive the part I need as of writing this review.

Builds and modding: It looks more tedious compared to warframe but you can get pretty far due to level based loot here having increased stats. I don't think you need to rely on upgraded modules until halfway through the story when you should start upgrading. Late game I'm unsure as I just reached it a few hours ago. Modules are also resource heavy and stat heavy at the last few levels.

Complete Bias and Worry for the Future: I have played multiple of Nexon's games such as The Finals, Dirty Bomb, Maple Story and Vindictus. This game included and all I can say is they have a HUGE focus on monetization and have historically made their games worse in future versions. Vindictus for example didn't have a stamina system when I played it over 10 years ago but more recently they added the stamina system that reduced or outright prevents you from gaining exp and resources from doing missions. GUESS what!!! you can pay premium currency to recover some of that bar back. This didn't really effect me as I rarely played BUT it's one of many examples that made the game more reliant on monetaization. Another was you can break and lose gear you've worked on for weeks when trying to upgrade them. You of course can buy premium stuff to prevent breaking and to recover your item. This lead to people Whaling for +20 weapons while F2P people remained at +5 at the highest. This also ruined late game a lot because if you paid enough I've seen people solo raids which require like 8 people. Whaling hard enough made you worth 8+ people which is incredibly unhealthy for the game and why most people left because future content catered to whales. Nexon generally has good settings and fine gameplay but the farming and monetization ruins them. Some of their failed games just don't have a lot of support from the company.

Overall this game is a solid 5/10. Not good or bad but the monetization and frustrating features need to be looked at so I worry for its future. Try to listen to the general playerbase and not the moneybags, Warframe and Destiny share similarities to this game and are still around many years later so Nexon also have other games to look at that are still fairly popular many years later. After the intro/honeymoon phase I'm sure there will be a decent to good amount of players remaining. Lets just hope Nexon doesn't fumble.

There is also optimization issues they haven't fixed since the playtest which is unfortunate and I hope they look into it.

UPDATE: Now I'm deep in end-game I've done most of the hard void intercept battles and have attempted to farm my 6th Descendant and WOW they are needlessly complicated. The later characters are insanely tedious to get so the early ones are deceptively easy and the void bosses I still haven't learned, my team just luckily dps through the gimmick and if not we get a guaranteed squad wipe.

Sunken cost fallacy might kick in but I urge you all to not pay Nexon. The late game gets exponentially worse.

External Components make a HUGE difference and not having a way to manipulate or change the extra effects or main stat means you'll almost never reach your full potential which is annoying and unreasonable to farm for.

Overall the game is a 3/10. The visuals and basic gameplay outside of bosses are alright but most things aren't done well or seen in a good light. Nexon without a doubt will focus on milking out money from the playerbase rather than producing a worthwhile product which is unfortunate. Hopefully they do better in the future.

A brief review of the 1st (easy) part of TFD from the casual

First and most importantly - I have never played „free-to-play“ co-op grinders like Warframe or Destiny before - my favorite games are single-player, leisurely Fallouts, Witchers and Cyberpunk, maybe Elden Ring (if you want to suffer).
1. TFD vs. Elden Ring 😊
(!) TFD captivated me with its gameplay, the lack of a plot as such, the variety of characters and their original combat features and mechanics. Well, and the ability to tumble, although this serves more of a decorative function (since bosses do not lose focus like in ER).
2. Characters
I started with Lepic, continued with Bunny, tried Frayne and Valby, and returned to Lepic again, pumping up the Thunder Cage to the 4th upgrade and 270k damage. Here we must make a reservation - all characters are good, but each one needs to be pumped from zero to level 40; it is not difficult if you use special operations and infiltration, but it is quite annoying for the surrounding party members.
3. Bunny
Also annoying for those around is the use of Bunny as a weapon of mass destruction - but here you need to come to terms with the reality. Bunny is the best character for grinding, but for bosses her basic shield and health are weak. (!) Bunny's build for bosses should have been implemented very carefully, with an emphasis on resistance and not exclusively on damage - constantly resurrecting them is not fun at all.*
* a typical picture of a fight for a boss performed by casuals - conditional Ajax and Lepiks are damaging, and Bunny is crawling around on all fours - beauty!
4. Hard phase
Having completed the game in easy mode, I got colossal pleasure ... which was immediately killed by the second boss in the hard phase. The Dead Bride has an indecent amount of health, and due to the "under-pumped" Character (Lepik 40!) and casual friends, it is impossible to take out the boss in 10 minutes. And here we come to the most controversial part of the gameplay - grinding for the ultimate weapon and characters.
5. Ultimate Grind
According to fans of grinders - this is where the fun begins. I disagree with the ultimate! If in ER Malenia takes you out in 30 seconds with a mimic and a super gun, you wipe yourself off and go on to level up. Or watch on YouTube how a character in his underwear takes her out with his clean fists in 2 minutes. In TFD, you stupidly (stupidly!) fight the theory of probability, not realizing that 6% does not mean that you will get the Super Lepic blueprint on the 17th attempt - not at all! it's depressing...
6. Summary
The first part is almost a masterpiece and is completed in one breath - this is if you develop 2-3 characters and a couple of favorite guns. Then everything depends on patience and free time. Of course, you can buy everything, no problem. But (!) then the eSports component disappears and it becomes sad. You can donate to the developers for skins – it is ok.
P.S. with the second part it is more difficult or I would say that the real business of the creators begins here. I don't know at the moment whether I can get Ultimate Lepic for free, but following the logic of the game, the creators assume that somewhere here I should open my wallet. What do you think?

Some of these reviews are hilarious.  People played for less than an hour leaving negatives.  You barely even get through the basic tutorial stuff in an hour.  People who have played 140+ hours leaving negative...  wow, you must REALLY hate the game to ONLY play 140 hours in the first week.  Then the negative because the guy with integrated Intel graphics can't run it.... don't even need to say anything.

It has been a fun game.  My hours at review are probably 20+ over from leaving the game open in the background overnight.  There is nothing "predatory" about the cash shop, you see one banner on launching the game about it (which you can turn off) and you are never once sent to the shop or run into a wall  that directs you to the shop.

You can play the entire game free.  That is probably 40-60 hours of going through the story and required missions along with it.  You get a free character to start, another right in the first few missions, a third by the end of the story and probably have the materials to create another character by the end of the story as well.  You also get 10 character slots free, so create characters from grinding out the materials all you want.  if you hit 10 characters all for free you would have about 150-200 hours in the game, and 5 more slots is $5.  That isn't much for a game you plan to keep playing after 150+ hours.

You get cash shop stuff in the free part of the season pass.  You also get free paints, emotes, titles, accessories and a few more things just for playing, located in your "journal".  

You do not have to spend a dime on the game.  And as far as the TOS, it is the same thing that EVERY WEBSITE YOU EVER GO TO ASKS via cookies.  You just say no you do not want to share that data.  The rest has been reviewed by multiple outlets and confirmed to be standard for a online game TOS.

The entire point is, the game is free.  Log in and check it out, if it is not for you then just uninstall.  I really cannot believe the entitlement of some of these kids reviewing the game that want a free game and want everything in it free too.  My guess is a LOT of kiddies who can't get mom or dad's credit card, so they are taking out their little temper tantrum on the reviews.  But this is what happens with a free game, every troll on the internet can install it and leave a review and you end up with endless trash reviews.

One note about Warframe...  a lot of these people are salty there is a new game out.  They sit in WF doing nothing all day long because they have been playing 11 years and have done it all.  They are the ones doing 49473 mid-air maneuvers per second in WF because that is all that game is, jumping around like a jacked up squirrel.  Destiny straight rips people off, and WF is just boring, especially when you get to the more complicated stuff and spend 9/10 of your time alt-tabbed watching Youtube to figure out how it works or where to get something (Also, First Descendant has a tab in-game where you can look up every single thing in the game and it will tell you where to get it and all the details about it, free).

Im gonna give my personal pros and con's on this game:

[b]Pros:[/b]
+categorized mods - as in warframe, this game has mods to enchance your [strike]warframe[/strike], i mean descandent  and weapons, but difference is that theres 4 weapon types - ones which use general, high-powered, special or impact bullets. The mods also categorized that way that the fire rate may not be for everyone but for specific ammo type weapon - i found that neat.
+grappling hook - no need for vehicles or other stuff because grappling hook gives you everything you need in terms of mobility, works just like grappling hook in just cause series - including grapple to enemies (no items to toss on em sadly)
+Simplified exploring - no need to scratch your head on what you wanted to do since quests go kinda linear
+hot joining - while exploring map, you can possibly join random player doing same mission by attacking his mission enemies or interacting with mission beacon so it can teleport you to ongoing mission if its somewhere active in map.

[b]Cons:[/b]
-All type of skin cosmetics are behind paywall, unless you willing to do battlepass or join occasional twitch drop farming. Don't care about it since im poor but prices are veeeery steep
[b]-Stability:[/b] This one is main reason i put game currently thumbs down - if you scroll a bit down you can see minimum and recommended specs to run this game. I say those specs are blatant lies - i have intel i5-6500, 16gb of ram and Geforce GTX 1070 and this game runs like hot crap, need at least "recommended" specs to be able run game on lowest graphic settings. 
During loading screens its preparing shaders for like 5 min, in some locations i need to wait loading time up to 10 min, what makes it worse that at around end of preparing shaders it simply crashes but its uncommon, altough i experienced blue screen of death twice due to how much cpu resources it eats (i probably spent 20% of my current review game time just watching loading screen). 
I tought would end about it here but it gets much worse the more you progress the game, currently im softlocked from main campaign story line due to "the shelter" quest and how enourmos resources it eats. I get crash all the time after i arrive at around the part where [spoiler]need protect thing in a middle and wait for it to be completed.[/spoiler]
If you think you can play this game with their description  of "minimum". [b]Don't[/b] or your computer (probably mostly cpu) gonna cry.
Oh and i couldn't modify games configs regarding graphics and stuff because i got denied of file access so there's that...
-confusing aspects or lack of tutorial: some parts of the game simply is straightfoward confusing, for example, the stealth mechanic aka "infiltration" - you can deactivate enemy generators by disabling them while enemies don't see you but enemy can see you instantly if you are for 1 second in their line of sight - zero explanation how it's done. One more example is missions where you can get resources by "activating mission with chill" or other elemental attributes, which turns out is not elemental modification of gun but elemental skill which is embedded to descendant - it cant be even switched with reactors (the thingy which enable your skills).
-No third person side switching, currently its stuck to right side.

I would gladly recommend the game if it recives perfomance fix or something so it becomes playable for me again but for now this game is definitely not low-end spec friendly.

edit 1: above text was review'd when i had around 13 hours game time (3 of them were waiting for loading screen to be done). Soooo now i have 158 hours in game, got used to playing on 15 fps, crashing seems to be less frequent now and i guess it has nice community since they let me afk some story missions because stability sucks and instead of crashing im getting perma screen freeze or even blue screen, but they are uncommon (every 3-5 hours on game). So i guess another pro that when you get used to it, its addicting.
